identity: An Arabic translation (credited to Amani Salem) of Leo Tolstoy's short story 'How Much Land Does a Man Need?' (kam min al-ard yahtaj al-insan). Register: abridged literary narrative in plain Modern Standard Arabic - the graded-reader / anthology-retelling voice, not high literary style. Structure: three front-matter lines (title; author byline 'qissat Leo Tolstoy'; translator credit 'tarjamat Amani Salem'), then 45 narrative paragraphs that alternate scene-narration with direct speech whose quotation marks and colons have been stripped along with all other punctuation. 48 paragraph segments in all, separated by the 47 literal <NL> tokens.
law: The sentence unit here is the narrative CLAUSE-CHAIN, not the clause. MSA narrative prose links independent predications with wa- / fa- / thumma, and those links are intra-sentential, so a connector-initial clause is presumed to CONTINUE the sentence; paragraphs of 30-52 tokens are routinely a single sentence in this text. A boundary is posited only where positive evidence defeats that presumption: (1) ASYNDETON - two complete predications juxtaposed with no connective at all, which this style essentially never does inside one sentence, so the mark removed there was terminal; (2) CLOSE OF DIRECT SPEECH followed by narration with a DIFFERENT subject - the quote is syntactically closed and the outer sentence complete, so the resumed narration is a new sentence even when it opens with fa- or wa-; (3) JUXTAPOSED COMPLETE UTTERANCES INSIDE a quotation (question after question, exclamative before assertion), where the removed mark was ? or !. Counter-rules that suppress boundaries: a speech frame plus its quote is ONE sentence, because the removed mark is a colon and a colon is not terminal - so never break after qala / qa'ilan / fa-sa'ala / wa-qala; the subordinators an, alladhi-allati, lakin, hatta, law, idha, kullama, lamma, bayna-ma, ma dama never open a sentence here; thumma is a pure coordinator (24 occurrences, paragraph-initial only twice and both times an <NL> had already forced the break); and wa- / fa-initial clauses that keep the SAME subject are continuations, including when they follow a closed quotation. Result: 34 of the 48 paragraph segments are exactly one sentence, 66 boundaries in all, averaging about 22 tokens per sentence.
reasoning: No doctrine file exists, so this is reasoned from the text alone. ANCHOR SITE, i=469 khiyamahum | tajamma'a: this 64-token paragraph is the longest in the document and it holds the only bare perfect verb that follows a complete predication with no connective whatsoever ('...until he reached where the Bashkir had pitched their tents | The Bashkir men gathered around Baaoum'). Asyndeton is undeniable here, and it calibrates everything else: since this text DOES juxtapose sentences without a connective, every other asyndetic junction is a boundary too. The same test carries i=525 (akhtaruha | qala al-za'im - two speech turns packed into one paragraph, the second frame verb bare), i=558 (biha | innana naqis al-ard bil-ayyam - the emphatic innana repeated with no wa-), i=1224 (wal-qub'a | lam yahtafiz illa bi-fa'sihi - a fresh negated predication interrupting the discard-chain), i=44 (shay'an | law annani amlik qit'at ard - a counterfactual wish opening asyndetically after a completed complaint; had it been one sentence the writer would have written wa-law), i=101 (ard | sawfa ashtari), i=1243 (al-shams | laqad afsadtu al-safqa bi-tam'i) and i=1434 (mutamayyiz | laqad hasalta 'ala arad kathira) - the two laqad assertions are the identical construction and must be graded alike. QUOTE-CLOSE SITES were the genuinely hard class, and I resolved them by subject continuity rather than by which particle happens to appear. Where the quote ends and narration resumes with a NEW subject I break: i=779 (laka | baraqat 'ayna Baaoum - asyndetic, hence certain), and by parity i=819 (chief speaks, then fa-wada'a Baaoum), i=599 (Baaoum speaks, then fa-dahika al-za'im) and i=1440 (chief speaks, then wa-asra'a khadimuhu). Where the SAME subject continues I do not break, which is why I rejected i=1073 (fa-qala innaha tasluh li-ziraat al-kattan ... wa-hafara hufra - Baaoum throughout), i=1113 (ikhtisar al-dil' al-thalith | thumma asra'a fi khutah) and i=1376 (fa-saha bi-jaza' da'at juhudi kulluha | wa-kada yataqaf): each reads cleanly as 'he said X, then he did Y', one sentence. Without this subject test the quote-close class would be all-or-nothing; with it the class splits 4 against 3 on a principled basis. IN-QUOTE PUNCTUATION SITES: at 536-548 Baaoum stammers three things with no connective at all - 'fi al-yawm | ayyu miqyasin hadha | kam hiktaran ta'ni'. The second junction (i=545) is two complete interrogatives side by side and is certain; the first (i=542) is an echoed fragment that most likely took ? or !, but a comma is conceivable, so med. Same shape but weaker at i=1193 (ah ya ilahi | madha af'al idha ta'akhkhartu) - the interjection is a complete exclamative and what follows is a complete question, yet a comma is about as likely as a !, so lo. i=395 (faqat | wa-adafa) is the one boundary I take on discourse rather than syntactic grounds: the report shifts from INDIRECT speech (wa-qala innahu ishtara) to DIRECT speech (wa-adafa: laqad 'aqadtu sadaqat), and that shift plus the 49-token span makes a full stop likelier than a comma; med, because wa-adafa can legitimately coordinate with wa-qala. REJECTED, and worth recording as the edge of the law: every wa-initial clause carrying no other evidence - i=199 (wa-kullama tajawwala fi ardihi), i=302 (wa-hunaka wajada), i=447 (wa-fi al-tariq ishtara), i=871 (wa-ba'da alf khutwa ukhra), i=1289 (wa-ra'a Baaoum rijal al-Bashkir), i=1366 (wa-fi nafs al-lahza) - and every fa-explicative - i=27, i=242 (fa-al-sha'ir yartafi'), i=339, i=563, i=1481 (fa-qad kana fi al-haqiqa la yahtaj). I also rejected i=144, where the subject shifts from the dual couple to Baaoum alone, because the shift sits inside a thumma-chain and thumma is 24-for-24 a coordinator here; and i=1231 (thumma akhadha yarkud) for the same reason, even though the break I posit at 1224 would license it. The residual risk is concentrated and correlated: if this corpus does NOT treat a closed quotation followed by narration as a sentence end, then 599, 819 and 1440 fall together; if it does not count ? or ! inside quotations, then 542 and 1193 fall together. Both classes are marked med or lo so that grading separates them cleanly from the asyndeton core, which I would defend at any confidence.
